items.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: If it wasn’t for Walter Quintus, who got me in tune, it would be unlistenable, Walter the engineer.

ctx.x: The theme is from the book. The book and the movie had nothing to do with long distance running. But I loved the image of the long distance runner and the idea of the artist as a long distance runner. This was a very programmatic – the race, going against the wall, breakaway, wall of pain. I interviewed runners. I found out what it is like. It’s just the idea of marathon runner. I couldn’t think of anything more out, racing for 26 miles or 26 kilometers, whatever it is. What a fascinating thing. It made me – it…
done. Everything is written out. I really worked on that, all soprano. If it wasn’t for Walter Quintus, who got me in tune, it would be unlistenable, Walter the engineer.
So basically, the tunes are all through-composed?
